paper.title: The Skein Hash Function Family
paper.venue: NIST SHA-3 competition submission, specification version 1.3 (1 October 2010)

program.how: written for ounce-core from Section 3 of the specification (Threefish, UBI, configuration block, output function); no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: the 13 precomputed initial chaining values of Appendix B (Skein-256 with 128/160/224/256-bit output, Skein-512 with 128/160/224/256/384/512, Skein-1024 with 384/512/1024) equal the state computed from the configuration block with Threefish and UBI
the 9 test vectors of Appendix C (Skein-256-256, Skein-512-512 and Skein-1024-1024, each on three messages FF, FF FE FD .. of 1, Nb and 2 Nb bytes) are reproduced
22 published values in all; the Round-2 rotation constants of the version 1.3 specification are used

expected_values_source.what: Appendix B (initial chaining values), Appendix C (test vectors) and Tables 3-4 (word permutation, rotation constants) and the constant C240 of the Skein specification v1.3
expected_values_source.note: values and tables are data, copied as numbers (extracted from the PDF text by a script); the submission package's reference code was not copied

negative_control: built with -DSKEIN_ROT0=15 (the first Threefish-256 rotation constant changed from 14 to 15), 15 of 22 values match (the Threefish-256 based ones fail) and the program exits 1
not_checked: security claims and the paper's analysis
tree hashing, MAC, key, personalization, nonce and other optional inputs (only simple hashing)
bit-granular messages (all vectors are whole bytes) and output lengths not listed in Appendix B / C
the NIST submission package's much longer known-answer files
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the 22 published Skein initial chaining values and test vectors of the v1.3 specification. It does not show the security claims hold.
